problem:
A particle $P$ is moving in the $x$-$y$ plane. Its position vector relative to a fixed origin $O$ is given by

$$
r=⟨3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)-5\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the velocity vector $v.$

$v=⟨${{field-1}}$\,,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-12\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)⟩$

feedback.problem:
A particle $P$ is moving in the $x$-$y$ plane. Its position vector relative to a fixed origin $O$ is given by

$$
r=⟨{t}^{3/2}+4{t}^{2},\,11t-1⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the velocity vector $v.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The particle's velocity vector is given by the derivative of its position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3/2}+4{t}^{2}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(11t-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{2}\sqrt{t}+8t,\,11⟩\end{aligned}
$$
